rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zacharias, elderly and surrounded by religiously indifferent relatives, feared leaving no heir to Jacob’s religious legacy and prayed for an heir to carry it.
rows.anchor: he was worried that he had no heir to the legacy of Jacob’s progeny he carried with himself

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling God the best heir does not mean religion depends on Zacharias’s family; God can raise others to serve it, while Zacharias only sought that his family retain this service.
rows.anchor: He Himself is the best heir of His religion.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zacharias’s legacy was the religion of Jacob’s descendants, not property; God answered his prayer with John because he sought a successor to serve religion.
rows.anchor: His legacy did not consist of wealth and assets, it consisted of the religion of Jacob’s progeny

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people praised in the verse are especially Zacharias’s immediate family; his broader paternal family was negligent toward religion.
rows.anchor: especially to the family of Zacharias (sws).

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God accepted the prayer because Zacharias’s family were not worldly slaves and competed in good deeds, a distinctive trait of Jacob’s progeny.
rows.anchor: they had the spirit of outdoing each other in righteousness, which was a distinct feature of Jacob’s progeny.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worldly people pray in hardship but, once rescued, attribute relief to their own planning and forget God.
rows.anchor: they regard it to be product of their own planning and forget Him

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Unlike hypocritical or idolatrous people who call on God only in distress, Zacharias’s family invoke Him in every circumstance, hopeful or despairing.
rows.anchor: they called upon God in all circumstances whether in hope or in despair.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their submission means they neither grow arrogant when favored nor become ungrateful and desperate when deprived.
rows.anchor: people are not ones who would become arrogant if they were blessed with favours and become ungrateful and desperate if they are deprived of them

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The chaste woman is Mary; she is left unnamed because the stated attribute identifies her uniquely, and she was treated in detail in Sūrah Maryam.
rows.anchor: This verse refers to Mary (sws) who has been mentioned in detail

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The expression about guarding her vulnerable organs is idiomatic: its coined overall meaning, not the literal wording, is intended.
rows.anchor: In these idioms, the literal meaning of the words is not implied; rather the overall meaning for which they have been coined is implied.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The idiom means keeping oneself clean from vice or protecting oneself from danger.
rows.anchor: he kept himself cleansed from every vice or protected himself from danger

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The same idiom is used for men as well as women.
rows.anchor: this idiom is used for women, it is also used for men.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Arabic word for the vulnerable organ also carries the sense of a place of fear.
rows.anchor: Arabic actually refers to ﻣﻮﺿﻊ ﻣﺨﺎﻓﺔ place of fear).

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s special command kun brought about the child in Mary’s womb, so the verse describes God as blowing His Spirit into him.
rows.anchor: blew His spirit into a child conceived in her womb.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jesus’s conception by command, beyond ordinary physical and biological laws, makes him and Mary signs of God.
rows.anchor: Jesus (sws) and his mother are from among the great signs of God.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Islahi says the Gospels show Jesus describing himself in the Qur’anic terms and argues that Paul’s followers distorted the account; he treats the issue in Āl-i ʿImrān.
rows.anchor: Jesus (sws) himself said the same words about himself as the Qur’ ān as stating, as is evident from the Gospels.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Islahi says followers of Paul distorted the account of Jesus’s conception and gave it a new interpretation.
rows.anchor: It is the followers of Paul who have distorted the while incident and given it a new interpretation.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Verse 21:92 summarizes the preceding account of the prophets; Islahi begins to connect discriminating among prophets with religious innovations, but the page breaks off mid-thought.
rows.anchor: This is the summary of the whole discussion after a mention of all the prophets.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When the Prophet recounted earlier nations to Quraysh’s affluent leaders, they mocked him as a storyteller and tried to turn their people away from him.
rows.anchor: they would try to lead away their masses by saying that this person has nothing but anecdotes of the past.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage rebukes the disbelievers’ carelessness, then reassures the Prophet not to lose hope: he is on the right path, they have strayed, and they will see their fate.
rows.anchor: he should not lose hope because of their stubbornness and arrogance; he is on the right path and these people have deviated from it

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even a warning calamity does not reform them; when it is removed, they return to their old ways.
rows.anchor: as soon as the calamity leaves them, they will return to their ill-ways

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage points to signs within people and around them to prompt reflection and end their indifference.
rows.anchor: the signs found within a human being and the ones outside him are referred to so that people should reflect

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In response to warnings, the disbelievers dismiss the messenger’s reminders as old stories.
rows.anchor: these people regarded all the warnings of the messenger to be anecdotes of the past.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The concluding challenge exposes their contradiction: they acknowledge and affirm truth, then state its opposite and go astray.
rows.anchor: on the one hand, they accept and declare the truth, but then they lose their senses and state what is the opposite

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening and following interrogatives express sorrow over the addressees’ conduct and rebuke them.
rows.anchor: The purpose of this and the succeeding interrogative statements is to express sorrow on the attitude of the addressees and to rebuke them.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word in the question refers to the Qur’an, whose evasion was mentioned in the preceding verse.
rows.anchor: here refers to the Qur’ ān, evasion from which is mentioned in the previous verse.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement is left incomplete because it expresses sorrow and rebuke.
rows.anchor: Since the statement here expresses sorrow and rebuke, it is left incomplete.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Islahi connects their inability to receive the Qur’an to 47:24, which says their hearts are bolted so its words cannot penetrate them.
rows.anchor: At another, the Qur’ān (47:24) states that their hearts have been bolted. For this reason, its words are not able to penetrate into them.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Being startled and diverted because revelation conflicts with ancestral custom is ignorant; inherited traditions are not automatically right and must accord with human nature and reason.
rows.anchor: These traditions in themselves are not necessarily correct. They must also conform to the norms of human nature and intellect.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham and Ishmael are the Quraysh’s true forefathers and preachers of this religion, so they should follow these noble ancestors rather than ancestors unaware of religion.
rows.anchor: Their real forefathers are Abraham (sws) and Ishmael (sws). They were proponents and preachers of this religion.
